newsitem.title: ITALY: No mini-budget would be suicidal for Italy - finmin.
newsitem.headline: No mini-budget would be suicidal for Italy - finmin.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on Tuesday that it would be "suicidal" for Italy not to pass a mini-budget to reach the goal of a three percent deficit to gross domestic product ratio required to join EMU.
"We would be mad or suicidal not to take the final step after all the efforts we have made," Visco told a parliamentary hearing.
Italy has already passed a stringent 1997 budget to try to achieve its goal of joining Europe's planned economic and monetary union at its launch in 1999.
Visco ruled out raising sales tax saying it would be unwise "both for inflation and because taxes should not be raised".

The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support gives Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government a parliamentary majority, has said it will not countenance tax hikes or welfare spending cuts in the forthcoming mini-budget.

The government has said the package will include structural measures and has deficit cuts of 14-15 trillion lire ($8.3-$8.9 billion). It is waiting for official state accounts, due to be published shortly, before unveiling the mini-budget.
